records.name: Short name
labels: Agent Slug (internal ID - used in filenames, API calls, consult_agent)
records.what: The agent's short name, in lowercase letters and hyphens. It is used for its folder and chat file, and when other agents or programs refer to it. Changing it renames all of those.
records.when: Change it only if the name is wrong or confusing. Reload the page afterward.
records.risk: Anything outside your Maestro that uses the old name, such as a program or a note, stops finding the agent. An agent that has call recordings cannot be renamed until they are downloaded and deleted.
records.def: Default: the name the agent was created with. We recommend keeping it.

records.name: Role
records.what: Sets what kind of agent this is: a team head you talk to (Primary), a specialist, a worker or an experimental agent. The role also decides what the agent may do without asking.
records.when: Make an agent Primary if it should lead a team and be the one you talk to. Leave helpers as specialists or workers.
records.risk: A team head is allowed more than a worker (it asks before sending things out instead of being refused), so give the role only to agents you trust. Lead powers are a separate box.
records.def: Default: specialist. We recommend leaving it unless the agent leads a team.
records.facts: lib/tool-policy.js:54-64 role defaults (worker/head/lead/member); roleOf lib/tool-policy.js ~roleOf: category 'primary' = head, lead:true = lead, anything else = worker. Default 'specialist when unset' is from the audit; code treats every non-primary category as worker for permissions. Stored as agents[].category. No restart (read per tool call).

records.name: Lead agent
records.what: Makes this agent the lead of your team. The lead can schedule tasks for other agents, see, change or cancel their tasks, and is the default agent for messaging channels.
records.when: Change it only if you want a different agent to run the team. Every agent can already schedule its own tasks without this.
records.risk: The lead has more reach than other agents, so choose it with care. Moving the lead changes which agent holds that wider access.
records.def: Default: off. We recommend one trusted lead and leaving the rest off.
records.facts: default off: lib/agents.js:249 (lead === true); changed per agent lib/agents.js:1747; code wins on 'gets root': not confirmed here, so the sentence says wider reach only. No restart: stored on the agent record, read per use (not traced further).

records.name: Short description
records.what: A one-line note about what this agent is for. It shows as a small pop-up when you point at the agent in a list.
records.when: Write one when you have several agents and want to tell them apart at a glance.

records.when: Change it when an agent should move to a different person, or when a member's agent should become a household one.
records.risk: The new owner can see and use the agent and its chats, and the old owner may lose access.

records.name: May search the web
labels: web (Action class: Web search and fetch)
records.what: Decides what happens when this agent wants to search or read pages on the web: it can just do it (allow), pause and ask you first (ask), or be refused (deny). It can follow the role's rule or have its own.
records.when: Set it to ask or deny for an agent that has no reason to go online. Set it to allow for a member's agent that needs the web.
records.risk: Allowing it lets the agent fetch pages from the internet. "Ask" only pauses if "Ask me before risky actions" is on; with that off, "ask" is treated as allow.
records.def: Default: follow the role (allowed for workers, team heads and the lead; refused for members' agents). We recommend leaving it.

records.risk: Allowing it lets the agent read files that may be private. "Ask" only pauses if "Ask me before risky actions" is on; with that off, "ask" is treated as allow.
records.def: Default: follow the role (allowed for workers, team heads and the lead; refused for members' agents). We recommend leaving it.

records.risk: Allowing it lets the agent change or overwrite files elsewhere. "Ask" only pauses if "Ask me before risky actions" is on; with that off, "ask" is treated as allow.

records.name: Administrator access
records.what: Lets you give this agent full administrator rights on your computer for a limited time (15 minutes up to 24 hours). Every administrator command it runs is written to a log.

records.risk: An agent with administrator rights can change or break almost anything on this computer. Only the lead agent has this by default; the grant ends by itself when the time is up.
records.def: Default: no grant. We recommend leaving it off and handing out short grants only when needed.

records.name: How Codex agents connect
records.what: Chooses how your Maestro talks to Codex agents. The normal way keeps one connection open and lets you step in mid-job. The older way starts a fresh run for each message.
records.when: Change it only if Codex agents fail to start and support told you to. Set it to exec for the older way.
records.risk: The older way is slower to take your interruptions, because each one runs as a follow-up. A wrong value is treated as the normal way.
records.def: Default: the normal way. We recommend leaving it.
records.facts: Env HUB_CODEX_TRANSPORT: exec selects the old way, anything else app-server lib/codex-cli/app-server.js:30-32; also falls back to exec when the app server fails to start lib/sdk-chat.js:6775-6779. Environment variable read from the hub's own environment, so it takes effect after a restart (not re-checked whether it is read per turn). No control on the page.

records.name: Codex approval level
records.what: Chooses when Codex agents must ask before running commands or changing files. The usual setting sends every non-trivial action through your Maestro's own safety rules.
records.when: Leave it alone. Set it to 'never' only if Codex agents are being stopped too often and you accept the risk.
records.risk: 'never' lets Codex run commands and change files without the extra check. Other values change how often it asks.
records.def: Default: the usual setting (untrusted: your Maestro's rules decide). We recommend leaving it.
records.facts: lib/codex-cli/index.js:351-358 HUB_CODEX_APPROVALS accepts never / untrusted / on-request / on-failure; anything else becomes untrusted; read from the environment when Codex runs, but the environment file is loaded at start, so a restart is needed (audit says yes; the per-turn read itself is not a restart).

records.name: Codex closed-box mode
records.what: Lets Codex agents use Codex's own protective box when they run commands. Without it, Codex agents run with full access to this computer.
records.when: Set it to 'workspace-write' or 'read-only' on a computer where Codex's own box works, especially if members use Codex agents.
records.risk: Codex's own box does not work on some Linux computers, and then every command fails. Left unset, Codex agents can touch anything the Maestro's user can.
records.def: Default: not set, which means full access (no box). We recommend setting it where it works, or giving the agent the Maestro's own box instead.
records.facts: lib/codex-cli/index.js:75-87: values read-only / workspace-write / danger-full-access; unset or anything else = danger-full-access (full host access), so the audit's default 'off' means no box; read-only workers always get read-only. lib/sdk-chat.js:6986-6992 a member's agent may not run with full access. The audit says it makes the box work 'for hub-hands agents'; the code says it is for Codex's own shell, hub-hands agents use the Maestro's box instead (code wins). Environment value, restart needed (audit says yes). lib/security-check.js:624-626 warns when Codex agents run without it.

records.when: Almost never. Raise it if short jobs are being queued when they could have waited.
records.risk: A long wait holds up the agent that asked. A short wait queues more requests.

records.name: Monthly spending cap
records.what: Sets how many dollars of pay-per-use spending all your agents together may use in a month. When it is used up, agents on pay-per-use models stop answering until the month starts again or you raise it; agents on a subscription or on this computer keep working.
records.when: Set it if you use pay-per-use models (API keys) and want a hard limit on the bill. Leave it empty for no limit.
records.risk: At the cap, pay-per-use agents cannot answer, so work that needs them waits. A reply already being written finishes first. Subscriptions and local models are never counted or stopped.
records.def: Default: empty, no monthly cap. We recommend setting one if you use pay-per-use models. You get one notice at 80% and one when it is reached.
